# Taking an Audio Walk Without Losing the Street

An audio walk can reveal ventilation hum, crossing signals, birds, delivery carts, and the changing acoustics of an arcade. It can also reduce awareness if recording controls demand constant attention.

## Alternate listening and noting

Stop at a safe edge, listen for one minute, then write the nearest, farthest, steady, and intermittent sounds. Avoid recording identifiable conversations. When moving, keep equipment simple and leave one ear available for traffic and other people.

## Map changes, not loudness alone

A narrow passage may feel intense because sound reflects, while an open plaza with a louder peak may be easier to interpret. Mark surfaces, shelter, and crowd density alongside impressions. Repeating the route at another hour separates a regular pattern from one delivery truck.

Accessible route planning, seating, and predictable exits remain relevant even when sound is the subject; the companion museum note provides that perspective.
